claims.statement: `ExecutorKind` enumerates every runtime the server can name — 'mock', 'opencode', 'codex', 'claude', 'hermes', 'gemini', 'editor', 'pi', 'atomic', 'remote', 'docker', 'deep-agent', and 'custom' — and the ExecutionEngine constructor always registers ten defaults (mock/opencode/codex/claude/hermes/gemini/editor/pi plus AtomicExecutor as 'atomic' and RemoteMakerExecutor as 'remote', the latter constructed with the database) while registering deep-agent only when DJIMIT_DEEP_ENABLED=true (also instantiating the DeepAgentContractIssuer).

`docker` and `custom` are never registered by the constructor: 'docker' only appears as the kind set by DockerSandboxExecutor in its constructor when the engine wraps another executor at dispatch time, and 'custom' is the extension slot for out-of-tree implementations added via registerExecutor(), which indexes executors by kind in a Map.

The TaskExecutor contract is `kind`, `start(task, options) → Promise<ExecutionSession>`, `canExecute(task) → boolean`, and optional `buildCommand(task, options) → { command, args }`; buildCommand is what lets DockerSandboxExecutor re-host an inner executor's CLI invocation without re-implementing argument construction.

ExecutionSession exposes `events: AsyncIterable<ExecutionEventCreateInput>` (persisted + broadcast by processEventStream), `result: Promise<ExecutionResult>`, `closed?: Promise<void>` (resolves only after the OS child and its streams close), mandatory `cancel()`, and optional, currently-unimplemented `pause()`/`resume()`.

ExecutionFailure carries `retryable` and `sideEffectsPossible`; the engine's normalizeFailure forces retryable=false whenever sideEffectsPossible is true, and nextRetryExecutor refuses any retry if attempt >= maxRetries, !failure.retryable, or failure.sideEffectsPossible — so post-side-effect failures never chain-hop providers.

All CLI adapters share runtime plumbing: runtime-process.ts (runtimeProcessClosed + SIGTERM→SIGKILL-after-5s stopRuntimeProcess that resolves on actual close), executor-env.ts (buildExecutorEnv allowlists safe env so server secrets stay out of spawned CLIs), captureExecutorOutput (5 MiB rolling stdout/stderr tail), and structured-runtime-event.ts (maps tool_use/tool_result/error/text JSON chunks from claude/gemini/editor/codex/opencode/pi into TOOL_CALL/TOOL_RESULT/ERROR/LOG events with usage).

The skip-permissions boundary is operator-armed: resolveExecutorSkipPermissions returns true only when task metadata requested it AND RUNTIME_ALLOW_SKIP_PERMISSIONS==='true', and ExecutionEngine.startExecutionAttempt only forwards skipPermissions to the adapter when that guard passes (a test asserts all four combinations). Per-executor * _SKIP_PERMISSIONS envs remain a second default layer.

DockerSandboxExecutor wraps an inner TaskExecutor, requires inner.buildCommand (else DOCKER_SANDBOX_INNER_COMMAND_UNAVAILABLE), reports kind:'docker', and enforces non-root user (1000:1000), --cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, read-only root + tmpfs /tmp (64 MiB), networkMode 'none' by default, cpu 1.0 / memory 512m, --rm cleanup, and a digest-pinned image (DOCKER_SANDBOX_IMAGE must contain @sha256:; DOCKER_SANDBOX_SKIP_DIGEST_CHECK=true bypasses with a warning and is NOT recommended for production). These invariants are asserted in docker-sandbox-executor.test.ts.

The engine creates a DockerSandboxExecutor inside startExecutionAttempt when task.metadata.sandbox.enabled===true, overriding image/cpu/memory/network/bind-mounts on DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG; deep-agent is explicitly forbidden from this Docker sandboxing path ('Deep Agent sandboxing is controlled by the sovereign runtime').

DeepAgentExecutor is gated on a signed contract: canExecute requires task.metadata.deep_agent_contract with identity.task_id matching this task and capabilities.profile_id==='no-tool-canary'; start() throws DEEP_AGENT_CONTRACT_INVALID_FOR_TASK otherwise. The remote transport accepts only an HTTP loopback or literal Tailscale IPv4 DJIMIT_DEEP_URL and fails closed on non-zero exit, timeout, oversized response, or unparseable final status.

deep-agent never participates in fallback: when its circuit breaker is open the engine throws instead of falling back, and nextRetryExecutor returns null for a failed deep-agent attempt — a contract-gated run is terminal by design.

CircuitBreakerService keeps per-ExecutorKind state CLOSED→OPEN→HALF_OPEN→CLOSED: CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD consecutive failures (default 3) in a 60s sliding window opens the circuit, canExecute returns false while OPEN until CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RECOVERY_MS (default 30s), then one probe is allowed in HALF_OPEN and 2 consecutive successes close it again.

FallbackChainService maps each ExecutionMode to an ordered provider list (fast: opencode→gemini→claude; standard: claude→codex→gemini; controlled: claude→codex; restricted: claude only) and getNextAvailable walks the chain after the current kind, skipping breakers that are open; custom chains can be injected via constructor or setChain().

maxRetries per attempt comes from ExecutionModePolicyService by mode (fast:1, standard:2, controlled:3, restricted:0), so even a retryable failure cannot chain-hop in restricted mode; fallbacks are re-admitted through the policy gate (fallbackAdmitted) and each hop is persisted with failureCode, failureDomain, retryable, and sideEffectsPossible.

The production Dockerfile pins @openai/codex@0.146.0, opencode-ai@1.18.10, and @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.282 globally and build-time-verifies them with git/codex/opencode/claude --version probes (L93-L94); adjacent layers install the gh CLI as a static per-arch .deb pinned via ARG GH_CLI_VERSION=2.100.0 (verified with gh --version) for GithubPrReviewService, and atomic-agent 0.6.5 as a release tarball pinned by per-architecture sha256 (ATOMIC_AGENT_SHA256_X64/ARM64) verified with sha256sum -c, unpacked to /opt/atomic-agent, symlinked into /usr/local/bin and verified with atomic-agent --version (L79-L89). At runtime GET /swarms/runtime-readiness treats only codex and opencode as production runtimes, checks their binary contracts and provider credentials, returns ready/blocked_reasons per runtime, and never starts a worker (starts_workers: false).

Before spawning a loop worker, LoopWorkerExecutorService probes the lease runtime via LoopService.getRuntimeContract(), records a start worker manifest with the contract, and if the contract is unavailable or status is not ok records a fail manifest with blocked_reasons runtime_contract_drift, fails the lease with runtime_contract_unavailable_or_drifted, and throws RUNTIME_CONTRACT_DRIFTED — no provider process is spawned against a drifted contract.

RuntimeCommandService.getRuntimeContract probes each CLI runtime listed in its PROBES table (codex, opencode, claude, gemini, editor, pi, atomic — each with a binEnv binary override, help arguments, and required json/cwd/headless flags; atomic's json flag is empty because it emits plain text) with a <bin> --version probe plus the per-runtime --help probe, marks the contract drifted when a required json/cwd/headless flag is missing from the help output, stamps a sha256 conformance contract_hash with named checks (runtime_available, contract_not_drifted, structured_events, usage_accounting, bounded_lifecycle), caches contracts keyed by runtime::command for LOOP_RUNTIME_CONTRACT_CACHE_MS (default 5s, clamped 500ms–60s), and persists each fresh probe to the runtime_contract_probes table.

The LoopService runtime contract set covers manual, mock, codex, opencode, claude, gemini, editor, and pi, exposed via getRuntimeContracts() at GET /loops/runtime-contracts; the manual runtime is always available (status ok, proof_class static) but LoopWorkerExecutorService.executeMaker rejects manual maker leases with MANUAL_MAKER_REQUIRES_HUMAN, and manual checkers require an explicit non-manual runtime to dispatch (CHECKER_RUNTIME_REQUIRED).

OpenCodeExecutor reports token usage and cost collected from NDJSON step_finish parts as tokenUsage/costDollars metrics on the ExecutionResult, and resolves an exit-0 run as failed with code VERIFICATION_FAILED (retryable: false, sideEffectsPossible: true) when a verification tool step (build_check/lint/test/typecheck or a bash command matching tsc/eslint/vitest/jest/pytest/…) reports failure.
CodexExecutor sums usage.input_tokens and usage.output_tokens from turn.completed NDJSON events into the result tokenUsage metric.

Before any policy work, a registered executor must pass runtime admission: executeTask calls admitRuntime immediately after the executor lookup and returns status 'denied' with RUNTIME_NOT_ADMITTED when refused; startExecutionAttempt re-checks admission for every attempt including each fallback hop, so a fallback chain is not a runtime-admission bypass.

Runtime admission is decided by checkAdmission against the repo-resident RUNTIME_ADMISSIONS ledger (execution/runtime-admission.ts): assessments are operator-reviewed and version-bound, self-attestation and RUNTIME/SHARED ownership of any authority (task, policy, approval, evidence, canonical_memory, worker_lifecycle, capability_registry, promotion) are critical rejections, a PASS gate without evidence_refs counts as NOT_PROVEN, FAIL on the critical gates licensing/reproducibility/supply_chain is an immediate REJECT, and only ADMIT, CONDITIONAL, or LEGACY_ADMITTED decisions can execute — with expiry enforcement (expires_at) and drift denial when the probed version does not match the admitted one.

admitRuntime reads the observed version from the most recent runtime_contract_probes row probed at or after engine boot (ENGINE_BOOT_ISO), never from the task or the runtime's own output; every decision is persisted as a task event carrying the assessmentRef, a refused admission is always recorded as a high-severity runtime_admission policy violation, and RUNTIME_ADMISSION_MODE=shadow records the denial and violation while letting the run proceed (the operator's rollback).

The RUNTIME_ADMISSIONS ledger ships an expiring LEGACY_ADMITTED record for every registered runtime — opencode@1.18.10, atomic@0.6.5, codex@0.146.0, claude@2.1.282, remote, mock, hermes, gemini, editor, pi, deep-agent — plus a REJECTed negative-control admission for 'openhuman'; runtime-admission.test.ts asserts both that every executor the engine registers passes checkAdmission and that openhuman never does.

AtomicExecutor (kind 'atomic') runs `atomic-agent run --cwd <dir> --max-steps <ATOMIC_AGENT_MAX_STEPS, default 40>` with the goal fed on stdin, first writing an idempotent `config set` (spawnSync, 15s timeout) describing an OpenAI-compatible provider (default Ollama Cloud) into a Djimitflo-owned state dir (DJIMITFLO_ATOMIC_STATE_DIR, default /data/atomic-agent); the API key env var defaults to OLLAMA_API_KEY but is overrideable via ATOMIC_AGENT_API_KEY_ENV and is explicitly passed through buildExecutorEnv even outside the allowlist; `--no-approval` is passed only when skipPermissions is armed; stdout is plain text, so the run reports no token usage (usage_source: 'unavailable') and the diff is the evidence.

RemoteMakerExecutor (kind 'remote') spawns no local process: given options.model as '<host>/<species>' (e.g. workstation/atomic@llama-router) and a HEAD that is an ancestor of origin/main, it enqueues (host, species, base_commit, prompt) into remote_maker_jobs and polls; a host-posted 'done' result's patch (capped at 2 MiB by MAX_PATCH_BYTES) is applied to the local worktree with git apply --whitespace=nowarn; an unclaimed job fails after REMOTE_MAKER_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_MS (default 45 min) and a claimed one after REMOTE_MAKER_TIMEOUT_MS (default 30 min) counted from the claim, and every cancellation stamps remote_maker_cancelled:<reason> into stderr for the lease's failure_reason.

getRuntimeContract takes conformance shortcuts for three runtimes instead of a binary probe: 'manual' is always available with proof_class 'static' (execution requires a human), 'mock' reports the deterministic in-process contract, and 'remote' availability mirrors only the REMOTE_MAKER_ENABLED=true flag since there is no local binary to probe (supports_timeout_kill true because the queued job can be cancelled).

Executors are not mediated through ToolBroker: the ExecutionEngine constructs a ToolBroker but CLI-internal tool calls never traverse it — task-level policy is enforced at admission time (risk classification, policy decision, governance gate, approval) before any process starts, a limitation stated in the README ('runtime enforcement limited to pre-execution').

OpenCodeExecutor collects metrics from NDJSON lines on both stdout and stderr with line-boundary buffering (partial lines held in metricsBuffer and flushed at close), records at most one verification failure per (tool, reason), and applies OPENCODE_MAX_RUN_TOKENS as an in-run brake that stops the child as soon as the summed step tokens exceed the cap.

The shadow-mode shipped-code scan (SHIPPED_CODE_SCAN_MODE) re-hashes the on-disk installs of the four Dockerfile-pinned runtimes — @anthropic-ai/claude-code, @openai/codex and opencode-ai under the global node_modules root, plus atomic at /opt/atomic-agent — storing a new shipped_code_scans row with a diff and a shadow shipped_code_scan judgment carrying an admission check whenever the content hash changes; it never changes an admission itself.

GET /health/runtimes returns one read-only runtime-health row per runtime (union of the admission ledger, recent worker leases, and runtime_contract_probes rows): admission decision with days to expiry, admitted vs observed version with a drift flag, last probe status and age, 30/90-day lease outcomes, gym species with a circuit-breaker flag, and a readiness classification (ok | reassess | retire_unused | keep_test_only | hold | rejected | unknown_runtime); a runtime without a probe reports 'no probe', never 'ok', and nothing in runtime-health changes an admission.

LoopWorkerExecutorService (executeMaker/executeChecker) records a 'start' worker manifest with gate_refs ['runtime_contract'] plus capacity/budget snapshots before every worker spawn, and when the contract is unavailable or drifted it records a 'fail' manifest with blocked_reasons ['runtime_contract_drift'], fails the lease with failure_reason runtime_contract_unavailable_or_drifted, and throws RUNTIME_CONTRACT_DRIFTED — so no provider process is ever spawned against a drifted contract.
